what_happened: Seed report's design question 1 hoped gate-cache-lib.sh's corpus-digest machinery could supply a touched-path diff for free; traced gate_cache_entry_write/read and confirmed the persisted cache entry stores only one opaque composite hash per gate, never per-file hashes -- there is nothing to diff. Had to fall back to the orchestrator's existing invocation_modified_files as the only real touched-path source, which lives outside this task's declared file_scope.

Mechanically traced a concrete cache-correctness risk: verify-deploy.sh's generic --skip-unchanged cache-write block (~line 2251) writes a cache entry for a gate whenever it ran clean, keyed by the gate's DECLARED corpus (whole @extensions tree for gate 8), with no awareness of whether gate8_run internally narrowed its own run-all.sh invocation via --only. If gate 8 is wired to narrow without a companion fix, a narrowed-but-clean pass would wrongly certify the full corpus as green, letting a later --skip-unchanged run skip gate 8 entirely. Recommended forcing GATE_DIRTY_LIST membership whenever gate8_run narrows, regardless of outcome, as a precondition for shipping the narrowing at all.

Seed report's '149 suites' figure (measured 2026-11-10) had drifted to 195 by 2026-11-16 (confirmed via a precise find-based per-extension tally matching run-all.sh's own discovery loop exactly). The 17-gate @extensions set and gate8's 662,462ms cost were unchanged.

Dispatch description's '17 of 28 gates declare @extensions' denominator has drifted: the live gate-registry.data now holds 29 gates. The 17-gate id set itself re-derived exactly as stated, and the 'all 149 suites' figure is 195 live (research report 02 had already corrected it). Corrections recorded in the plan's Carried-Figure Re-Validation table.

Research report 02 had already traced the generic --skip-unchanged cache-write hazard to a specific code path and ruled out the gate cache as a touched-path source, so planning needed no re-investigation of either; the plan phases map almost one-to-one onto its recommendations. Plan validated clean (0 warnings) on first validate-artifact.sh run, including the Tier Justification measurement check.
